contains 2% or less of__food.analysis: {"name":"Contains 2% or less of","riskLevel":"low","summary":"This is not an ingredient but a labeling phrase indicating that the following ingredients each make up 2% or less of the product by weight.","details":"Food labels often use the phrase \"contains 2% or less of\" to group minor ingredients that are present in very small amounts. The health impact depends entirely on the specific ingredients listed after this phrase, not on the phrase itself.","category":"Labeling phrase / not an ingredient"}

glycerin__food.analysis: {"name":"Glycerin","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Glycerin (glycerol) is a common humectant and sweet-tasting compound used to retain moisture and improve texture in foods.","details":"Glycerin is generally recognized as safe (GRAS) and is widely used in processed foods, candies, and baked goods to keep them soft and moist. In typical food amounts it poses little risk for most people, though very high intakes may cause mild digestive upset (such as gas or loose stools) in some individuals due to its osmotic effect.","category":"Humectant / texture agent"}

cocoa processed with alkali__food.analysis: {"name":"Cocoa processed with alkali","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cocoa processed with alkali (Dutch-processed cocoa) is cocoa that has been treated with an alkaline substance to reduce acidity and create a milder flavor and darker color.","details":"The alkalization process makes cocoa smoother and less bitter, which is desirable in many chocolate-flavored foods and beverages. While this processing can reduce some natural cocoa flavonoids (beneficial antioxidants), it does not generally introduce major health risks; overall health impact depends more on the total sugar, fat, and other ingredients in the final product.","category":"Processed cocoa / flavoring"}

baking__food.analysis: {"name":"Baking","riskLevel":"low","summary":"“Baking” on its own is not an ingredient but likely part of the term “baking soda” or “baking powder.”","details":"In an ingredient list, the word “baking” by itself is incomplete and probably refers to a leavening agent such as baking soda or baking powder, which help doughs and batters rise. There is no specific health risk associated with the term alone; the actual risk depends on the complete ingredient (for example, baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, while baking powder can also contain added sodium and other components).","category":"Label artifact / likely part of leavening agent"}

hydrogenated (as in hydrogenated oils/fa.analysis: {"name":"Hydrogenated (as in hydrogenated oils/fats)","riskLevel":"high","summary":"Refers to fats that have been chemically hydrogenated, often creating trans fats that are strongly linked to heart disease.","details":"Hydrogenation is a process that adds hydrogen to liquid vegetable oils to make them more solid and shelf‑stable. This process can create trans fats, which raise LDL (bad) cholesterol, lower HDL (good) cholesterol, and increase the risk of cardiovascular disease and inflammation. When you see “hydrogenated” in an ingredient list (especially “partially hydrogenated oils”), it usually signals the presence of unhealthy industrial trans fats, even if the label rounds them down to 0 g.","category":"Trans fats / hydrogenated oils"}

mono (as in mono-glycerides)__food.analysis: {"name":"Mono (as in mono-glycerides)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Monoglycerides are emulsifiers made from glycerol and fatty acids, often derived from vegetable oils or animal fats.","details":"Monoglycerides help blend fats and water in processed foods like baked goods, margarine, and ice cream, improving texture and shelf life. Health concerns include that they can be a source of additional industrial trans fats, since they may be produced from partially hydrogenated oils, even though they are not counted in the ‘trans fat’ line on nutrition labels. For most people they are considered generally safe at typical intake levels, but those trying to strictly avoid trans fats or highly processed additives may wish to minimize them.","category":"Emulsifier / processing aid"}

diglycerides (as in mono- and diglycerid.analysis: {"name":"Diglycerides (as in mono- and diglycerides)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Diglycerides are emulsifiers similar to monoglycerides, used to improve texture and stability in processed foods and can also carry hidden trans fats.","details":"Diglycerides are molecules made from glycerol and two fatty acids, commonly added to foods to keep ingredients from separating, making products softer and extending shelf life. Like monoglycerides, they may be manufactured from partially hydrogenated oils, which means they can contribute small amounts of industrial trans fats that are not reflected in the nutrition facts panel. While regulatory bodies generally consider them safe, people limiting processed foods, trans fats, or certain animal-derived ingredients may prefer to avoid frequent consumption.","category":"Emulsifier / processing aid"}

soybean and wheat__food.analysis: {"name":"Soybean and wheat","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Soybean and wheat are common food ingredients that are major allergens and sources of protein and carbohydrates. They are generally safe for most people but can cause serious reactions in those with soy or gluten/wheat allergies or intolerances.","details":"Soybeans provide plant-based protein and fats, while wheat is a staple grain rich in carbohydrates and gluten. For individuals with soy allergy, wheat allergy, celiac disease, or non-celiac gluten sensitivity, consumption can trigger symptoms ranging from digestive distress to severe allergic reactions. For people without these conditions, these ingredients are usually safe, but they do indicate the presence of common allergens that some consumers need to avoid carefully.","category":"Allergens (soy, gluten/wheat)"}

ingredients (label marker not an ingredi.analysis: {"name":"Ingredients (label marker, not an ingredient)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"The word \"INGREDIENTS\" is a labeling header, not a consumable substance. It carries no nutritional or health risk on its own.","details":"Regulatory labeling standards require manufacturers to list components of a product under an \"Ingredients\" heading. This term is purely informational and indicates the start of the ingredient list, so it does not have any direct health impact or risk profile.","category":"Labeling / non-ingredient"}

bioengineered food ingredients (gmos)__f.analysis: {"name":"Bioengineered food ingredients (GMOs)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Bioengineered food ingredients indicate the presence of genetically modified organisms (GMOs). Current evidence suggests they are generally safe to eat, but some consumers have environmental, ethical, or precautionary concerns.","details":"The phrase \"contains bioengineered food ingredients\" is a regulatory disclosure that some components are genetically modified, often crops like soy, corn, or canola. Large scientific bodies (such as the WHO and major national academies) have not found consistent evidence that approved GMOs pose greater health risks than conventional counterparts. However, GMO use is sometimes associated with higher pesticide use or certain agricultural practices, and long-term ecological and sustainability issues remain points of debate, which leads some people to avoid them as a precaution or for personal preference.","category":"Genetically modified / bioengineered"}

food starch modified__food.analysis: {"name":"Food starch, modified","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Modified food starch is a processed form of starch used to thicken, stabilize, or improve the texture of foods and is generally considered safe for most people.","details":"Modified food starch is typically derived from corn, potato, tapioca, or wheat and then physically or chemically treated so it behaves better in processed foods (e.g., stable when heated, frozen, or under acidic conditions). For most consumers it poses low health risk, but sensitive individuals (such as those with celiac disease or wheat allergies) may need to verify the source if it is not specified, and some people prefer to limit highly processed additives in their diet.","category":"Food additive – thickener/stabilizer"}

mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids__f.analysis: {"name":"Mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Emulsifiers derived from glycerol and fatty acids, often used to improve texture and shelf life in processed foods.","details":"Mono- and diglycerides are commonly produced from vegetable oils, but can also be derived from animal fats or partially hydrogenated oils, which may introduce small amounts of trans fats. For most people they are considered safe at typical intake levels, but those aiming to strictly minimize processed additives, avoid all trans fats, or who follow certain religious/ethical dietary rules may want to limit them or verify their source.","category":"Emulsifier / food additive"}

bleached (refined bleached flour)__food.analysis: {"name":"Bleached (refined bleached flour)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Bleached flour is wheat flour treated to appear whiter and have a softer texture, often used in baked goods. It is generally safe for most people but is a source of gluten and is more processed and less nutritious than whole-grain flour.","details":"Bleached flour is typically treated with bleaching agents (such as benzoyl peroxide or chlorine-based agents) to speed aging and improve baking properties; these agents are used in very small amounts and are considered safe by regulators, but they indicate a higher level of processing and nutrient loss compared with whole-wheat flour. It contains gluten, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity, and its refined nature means it has less fiber and micronutrients and can contribute more to blood sugar spikes than less processed grains.","category":"refined grain / processing aid"}

malted barley flour__food.analysis: {"name":"Malted barley flour","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Malted barley flour is a ground form of sprouted barley used in small amounts to improve flavor, color, and yeast activity in baked goods. It is generally safe but does contain gluten.","details":"Because it is made from barley, malted barley flour naturally contains gluten and is not appropriate for people with celiac disease or non-celiac gluten sensitivity. In typical use levels in bread and cereals, it mainly serves as an enzyme and flavor source and is not associated with specific toxic or additive-related risks for the general population, though it remains a gluten-containing grain for labeling and allergen considerations.","category":"cereal grain / gluten source"}

niacin (vitamin b3)__food.analysis: {"name":"Niacin (vitamin B3)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Niacin is vitamin B3, commonly added to enriched flours and cereals to restore or boost nutrient content. At levels used in fortified foods, it is safe and beneficial for most people.","details":"Niacin is an essential vitamin involved in energy metabolism and nervous system function, and fortification helps prevent deficiency in populations that rely on refined grains. Adverse effects such as skin flushing, itching, or liver strain occur mainly with high-dose supplements, not with the relatively low amounts typically present in enriched or fortified foods.","category":"vitamin / nutrient fortification"}

myristamidopropyl betaine__skincare.analysis: {"name":"Myristamidopropyl Betaine","riskLevel":"low","summary":"A mild amphoteric surfactant used for cleansing and foam boosting, generally well tolerated by skin and hair.","details":"Myristamidopropyl betaine is a coconut- or myristic-acid–derived surfactant commonly used in shampoos, facial cleansers, and body washes to provide gentle cleansing and improve foam. It is considered milder than many sulfates (like SLS/SLES) and is usually suitable for sensitive skin, though a small number of people may experience irritation or contact allergy. It is not a paraben, sulfate, phthalate, formaldehyde-releasing preservative, silicone, mineral oil, or drying alcohol.","category":"Surfactant / Cleansing agent"}

polyquaternium-7__skincare.analysis: {"name":"Polyquaternium-7","riskLevel":"low","summary":"A conditioning polymer that improves slip, softness, and reduces static on hair and skin.","details":"Polyquaternium‑7 is a cationic polymer frequently used in shampoos, conditioners, and body washes to leave a smooth, conditioned feel and to reduce frizz and tangling. It has a good safety profile and is generally non-irritating at typical use levels, though it can build up on hair and may be problematic for those who strictly avoid film-forming ingredients. It is not associated with hormone disruption, is not a sulfate, phthalate, paraben, formaldehyde releaser, mineral oil, silicone, or drying alcohol.","category":"Conditioning polymer / Film former"}

sodium benzoate__skincare.analysis: {"name":"Sodium Benzoate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"A widely used preservative that helps prevent microbial growth; usually safe but can rarely cause irritation or sensitivity.","details":"Sodium benzoate protects water-based skincare and haircare products from mold and bacteria, improving shelf life and safety. At typical cosmetic concentrations it is considered low risk and is generally well tolerated, though some individuals with very sensitive skin may experience stinging or mild irritation, especially on compromised skin. It is not a paraben, does not release formaldehyde, and is not a sulfate, phthalate, silicone, mineral oil, or drying alcohol, but in formulas with ascorbic acid (vitamin C) under certain conditions it can theoretically form small amounts of benzene, which manufacturers manage by controlling formulation and storage conditions.","category":"Preservative"}

sodium chloride (table salt)__skincare.analysis: {"name":"Sodium Chloride (table Salt)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Common salt used mainly to adjust product thickness and sometimes for mild cleansing; generally very safe.","details":"Sodium chloride is used in shampoos and cleansers to modify viscosity and can have a slight cleansing or exfoliating effect at higher levels. It is considered low risk, though in high concentrations it may be drying or irritating, especially on compromised or very sensitive skin or on the scalp in people with conditions like eczema. It is not related to parabens, sulfates (SLS/SLES), phthalates, formaldehyde-releasing preservatives, silicones, mineral oils, or drying alcohols.","category":"Viscosity modifier / Bulking agent"}

fragrance (daily-use fragrance)__skincar.analysis: {"name":"Fragrance (daily-use Fragrance)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"A mixture of aromatic compounds added for scent; a common source of skin irritation and allergies despite being widely used.","details":"“Fragrance” (or “parfum”) is an umbrella term that can include dozens of natural and synthetic aromatic chemicals, some of which are known allergens or sensitizers. While many people use fragranced skincare and haircare without issues, those with sensitive skin, rosacea, eczema, or a history of allergies may experience redness, itching, or dermatitis, and the exact components are often not fully disclosed. Fragrance is not a paraben, sulfate, or formaldehyde-releasing preservative by definition, but certain fragrance ingredients or solvents can sometimes be associated with additional concerns, which is why fragrance-free or low-fragrance products are often preferred for sensitive or reactive skin.","category":"Fragrance / Potential allergen"}

dried (unspecified)__food.analysis: {"name":"Dried (unspecified)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"“Dried” alone is not a specific ingredient but a processing state, so it does not indicate any particular health risk by itself.","details":"The term “dried” usually describes an ingredient that has had most of its water removed (e.g., dried fruit, dried vegetables, dried herbs), but without the base food named, its health impact cannot be properly evaluated. Drying itself is generally a low‑risk preservation method, though some dried foods may also contain added sugars, salts, sulfites, or other additives, which would determine the actual risk level.","category":"Processing descriptor"}

sal__food.analysis: {"name":"Sal","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"La sal de mesa es necesaria en pequeñas cantidades, pero un consumo elevado se asocia con hipertensión y mayor riesgo cardiovascular.","details":"La sal aporta sodio, un mineral esencial para el equilibrio de líquidos y la función nerviosa y muscular. Sin embargo, cuando se consume en exceso, puede contribuir al aumento de la presión arterial, retención de líquidos y mayor riesgo de enfermedades cardiovasculares y renales. Las personas con hipertensión, problemas cardíacos o retención de líquidos deben limitar especialmente su ingesta de sal y revisar el contenido de sodio de los productos procesados.","category":"Alto contenido de sodio"}

葡萄糖__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"葡萄糖","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"葡萄糖是一种单糖，是常见的能量来源和甜味成分。适量摄入一般安全，但过量会增加血糖和能量摄入负担。","details":"葡萄糖升糖速度较快，血糖控制不佳者（如糖尿病或胰岛素抵抗人群）需要特别注意摄入量。长期大量摄入高糖食品与体重增加、蛀牙及代谢综合征风险升高有关。它不是人工甜味剂，也不是常见过敏原，但应放在整体饮食糖摄入框架下考量。","category":"糖类/甜味剂"}

蔗糖脂肪酸酯__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"蔗糖脂肪酸酯","riskLevel":"low","summary":"蔗糖脂肪酸酯是一种常用的食品乳化剂和稳定剂，用于改善食品口感与结构。一般认为在正常摄入量下较为安全。","details":"蔗糖脂肪酸酯通常由蔗糖和植物油中的脂肪酸制成，可用于烘焙食品、饮料、乳制品替代品等，帮助油水混合和保持均匀质地。大多数权威机构认可其安全性，但过量摄入可能引起部分人轻微消化不适。对于总体饮食健康，更应关注整体添加剂数量和饮食均衡。","category":"食品添加剂 / 乳化剂"}

无水葡萄糖（右旋葡萄糖）__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"无水葡萄糖（右旋葡萄糖）","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"无水葡萄糖是一种快速被吸收的单糖，用作甜味剂和能量来源。对血糖敏感人群（如糖尿病患者）需特别注意摄入量。","details":"无水葡萄糖会迅速进入血液，导致血糖水平短时间内明显升高，因此频繁或大量摄入可能增加肥胖、胰岛素抵抗和代谢综合征等风险。对于一般健康人，适量摄入通常不致产生直接危害，但高糖饮食整体上与心血管疾病和龋齿等问题相关。建议从全食物中获取碳水化合物，并限制各类添加糖的总摄入。","category":"糖类 / 甜味剂"}

香蕉__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"香蕉","riskLevel":"low","summary":"香蕉是一种天然水果，营养价值较高，一般人群食用安全性较高。","details":"香蕉富含钾、膳食纤维和维生素B族，不含人工添加剂、防腐剂或人工色素等成分。对大多数人来说适合作为健康零食，但对极少数对香蕉过敏或需严格控制钾摄入（如严重肾功能不全）的人群需适量或遵医嘱食用。","category":"天然水果"}

加工蜂蜜__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"加工蜂蜜","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"加工蜂蜜通常经过加热和过滤，口感稳定但部分活性成分可能减少，同时含糖量较高。","details":"与生蜂蜜相比，加工蜂蜜可能因加热而损失部分酶类和抗氧化物质，但其仍然主要由果糖和葡萄糖等单糖组成，升糖指数较高，不适合糖尿病患者或需要控制血糖、体重的人群大量食用。市售加工蜂蜜还可能掺入糖浆等成分，长期过量摄入易增加龋齿、肥胖和代谢问题风险，且1岁以下婴儿不应食用任何形式蜂蜜，以避免肉毒杆菌中毒风险。","category":"含糖甜味剂"}

酶制剂__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"酶制剂","riskLevel":"low","summary":"酶制剂是用于分解淀粉、蛋白质或脂肪等成分的加工助剂，常见于烘焙、乳制品和饮料中。正常摄入量下对大多数人来说安全性较高。","details":"食品中标注的“酶”通常作为加工助剂，在生产过程中起作用，最终成品中残留量很低。极少数人（如职业接触者）可能对某些特定酶产生过敏反应，但普通消费者日常饮食中接触的剂量一般非常低。整体来看，常规使用水平下的健康风险较低。","category":"食品加工助剂"}

食盐__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"食盐","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"食盐主要成分为氯化钠，是常见的调味品和防腐剂。少量摄入是人体必需，但过量会增加健康风险。","details":"长期高盐饮食与高血压、心血管疾病及肾脏负担增加等健康问题密切相关，因此加工食品中含盐量偏高时需要特别注意总摄入量。对于高血压患者、心血管疾病风险人群或需要限钠饮食的人群，更应控制含盐食品的摄入频率和份量。","category":"调味料 / 矿物盐"}

洋葱碎__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"洋葱碎","riskLevel":"low","summary":"洋葱碎是将新鲜洋葱切碎并干燥后的产品，一般作为调味配料使用。对大多数人来说较为安全。","details":"洋葱本身含有一定的含硫化合物和天然抗氧化物质，通常不会额外添加防腐剂或人工添加剂。少数对葱蒜类敏感或有胃肠道问题的人可能出现腹胀或不适。总体而言，它属于天然植物性调味食材，安全性较高。","category":"天然香辛料 / 蔬菜配料"}

天然香料__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"天然香料","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"天然香料通常是从植物或动物来源中提取的风味物质，用于增强食物的味道和香气。标签上往往不会详细列出具体成分。","details":"虽然标注为“天然”，但其提取和加工过程仍可能较为复杂，且不同来源的过敏原信息不透明，如可能含有乳制品、大豆或坚果来源成分。对过敏体质或对配料成分要求严格的人（如对谷氨酸盐敏感者）可能需要谨慎，因为“天然香料”作为统称，难以判断具体物质及其用量。总体风险中等，主要来自成分不透明和潜在过敏风险。","category":"香料 / 风味增强成分"}

洋葱提取物__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"洋葱提取物","riskLevel":"low","summary":"洋葱提取物一般来源于天然洋葱，用于增添香味与风味，整体安全性较高。","details":"洋葱提取物通常通过浓缩或提取洋葱中的风味成分制成，不涉及常见人工色素或甜味剂。少数对葱蒜类敏感或有胃肠道不适的人，摄入较多时可能出现胀气或轻微不适。对一般人群来说，在食品中作为调味成分使用，风险较低。","category":"天然调味成分"}

sal__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Sal","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"La sal es una fuente principal de sodio en la dieta; su consumo elevado se asocia con presión arterial alta y riesgo cardiovascular. En cantidades moderadas es necesaria para funciones básicas del organismo.","details":"Un consumo excesivo de sal puede contribuir a hipertensión, retención de líquidos y aumentar el riesgo de enfermedades cardiovasculares, especialmente en personas sensibles al sodio. En un producto procesado, la sal suele ser una de las mayores fuentes de sodio total, por lo que es importante considerar la cantidad por porción y en el contexto de toda la dieta diaria.","category":"Condimento / alto en sodio"}

almidón de maíz__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Almidón de Maíz","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El almidón de maíz es un espesante derivado del maíz, utilizado para dar textura a alimentos y salsas. Generalmente se considera seguro para la mayoría de las personas.","details":"Suele ser bien tolerado, pero en algunos casos puede proceder de maíz modificado genéticamente, lo cual puede preocupar a quienes buscan productos no transgénicos. Normalmente no contiene gluten, por lo que suele ser apto para celíacos, salvo riesgo de contaminación cruzada. Aporta principalmente carbohidratos refinados y casi ningún valor nutricional adicional.","category":"Espesante / carbohidrato refinado"}

especias__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Especias","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Las especias son mezclas de partes secas de plantas usadas para aportar sabor y aroma a los alimentos. En la mayoría de los casos son seguras y pueden tener compuestos beneficiosos.","details":"El término “especias” es genérico y no especifica cuáles se utilizan, por lo que es difícil valorar alérgenos concretos (como apio, mostaza o pimienta negra) que algunas personas sensibles deben vigilar. Normalmente no implican aditivos artificiales, aunque en mezclas procesadas podrían contener trazas de sal u otros componentes. Suelen emplearse en pequeñas cantidades, por lo que el impacto sobre la salud es limitado salvo en personas alérgicas.","category":"Condimento / saborizante natural"}

ajo__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Ajo","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El ajo es un condimento natural muy utilizado que aporta sabor intenso y posibles beneficios cardiovasculares. En la mayoría de las personas se considera un ingrediente seguro.","details":"Contiene compuestos sulfurados con propiedades antioxidantes y potencial efecto cardioprotector, aunque en productos procesados la cantidad suele ser baja. Puede causar molestias digestivas o malestar en personas con estómago sensible o con intolerancia específica al ajo. No se asocia a aditivos artificiales relevantes cuando se usa simplemente como ajo en polvo o deshidratado.","category":"Condimento / vegetal aromático"}

leche entera en polvo__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Leche Entera En Polvo","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Ingrediente lácteo completo deshidratado, nutritivo pero alergénico. Aporta proteínas, grasas y lactosa.","details":"La leche entera en polvo contiene caseína, suero lácteo y lactosa, por lo que es un alérgeno importante para personas con alergia a la leche o intolerancia a la lactosa. Su contenido de grasa saturada puede ser relevante en dietas con restricción de grasas, aunque en porciones habituales suele ser aceptable. No es un aditivo problemático en sí, pero debe evitarse en personas con alergia a proteínas lácteas o con intolerancia marcada a la lactosa.","category":"Lácteo / Alérgeno"}

pasta de tomate__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Pasta de Tomate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"La pasta de tomate es un concentrado de tomate con alto contenido de licopeno y otros antioxidantes naturales. Generalmente es un ingrediente seguro y nutritivo cuando no lleva exceso de sal ni aditivos problemáticos.","details":"Suele obtenerse por cocción y concentración del tomate, conservando vitaminas, minerales y compuestos antioxidantes. El principal aspecto a vigilar es el contenido de sodio cuando se le añade sal, así como la presencia de azúcares añadidos en algunas formulaciones comerciales. Para personas sensibles a la acidez gástrica o al reflujo, un consumo elevado puede causar molestias digestivas.","category":"Derivado de hortalizas"}

leche fermentada__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Leche Fermentada","riskLevel":"low","summary":"La leche fermentada es un producto lácteo con bacterias beneficiosas que pueden apoyar la salud intestinal. Es segura para la mayoría de las personas, pero contiene lactosa y proteínas lácteas que pueden causar problemas en personas intolerantes o alérgicas.","details":"La fermentación reduce parcialmente la lactosa y produce compuestos que pueden mejorar la digestión y el perfil de la microbiota intestinal. Sin embargo, sigue siendo un alérgeno lácteo importante y no es adecuada para personas con alergia a la proteína de la leche, y puede causar síntomas en intolerantes a la lactosa, según el grado de fermentación. También puede contener azúcar añadido en algunas versiones comerciales, lo que incrementa su aporte calórico y de azúcares libres.","category":"Producto lácteo fermentado"}

ácido cítrico__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Ácido Cítrico","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El ácido cítrico es un aditivo alimentario usado comúnmente como acidulante y conservante. En general se considera seguro para la mayoría de las personas.","details":"Se encuentra de forma natural en cítricos, pero en la industria suele producirse por fermentación. Puede causar molestias digestivas leves o irritación en personas muy sensibles o con estómago delicado, especialmente en grandes cantidades. No se asocia de forma relevante con alergias graves ni con efectos crónicos en la población general.","category":"Aditivo alimentario / Regulador de acidez y conservante"}

mono y diglicéridos de ácidos grasos__fo.analysis: {"name":"Mono y Diglicéridos de Ácidos Grasos","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Los mono y diglicéridos son emulsionantes derivados de grasas usados para mejorar textura y estabilidad de los alimentos. Su seguridad general es aceptada, pero pueden aportar grasas de origen poco claro y trazas de grasas trans.","details":"Se obtienen normalmente a partir de aceites vegetales, aunque a veces pueden proceder de grasas animales si el fabricante no especifica lo contrario. Al ser productos procesados, pueden contener pequeñas cantidades de grasas trans y contribuir ligeramente al aporte total de grasa, aunque en dosis bajas. Para una dieta muy controlada en grasas procesadas o en contextos de enfermedades cardiovasculares, se recomienda moderar el consumo de productos muy ricos en emulsionantes.","category":"Aditivo alimentario / Emulsionante derivado de grasas"}

cacao en polvo (procesado con álcali)__f.analysis: {"name":"Cacao En Polvo (procesado Con Álcali)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El cacao en polvo procesado con álcali (cacao holandés) se utiliza para mejorar el sabor y el color, y se considera generalmente seguro. El proceso con álcali reduce parte de los antioxidantes naturales del cacao.","details":"El tratamiento con álcali neutraliza la acidez del cacao, haciéndolo más suave y menos amargo, pero disminuye su contenido de flavonoides, que son compuestos beneficiosos. En personas sensibles a la cafeína o a la teobromina, el cacao puede causar nerviosismo leve o interferir con el sueño si se consume en exceso. También puede ser un problema para personas con alergia específica al cacao.","category":"Ingrediente alimentario / Derivado del cacao"}

glucosa__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Glucosa","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Es un tipo de azúcar simple que se utiliza como edulcorante y fuente rápida de energía en alimentos procesados.","details":"En cantidades moderadas, la glucosa es metabolizada de forma normal por el organismo, pero su consumo elevado se asocia a aumentos de glucemia, riesgo de resistencia a la insulina y problemas metabólicos en el largo plazo. Las personas con diabetes o con alteraciones de la glucosa deben vigilar especialmente su ingesta. Además, en productos procesados suele contribuir al contenido total de azúcares, favoreciendo el exceso calórico y el riesgo de caries.","category":"Azúcar / carbohidrato simple"}

ésteres de ácidos grasos de sacarosa__fo.analysis: {"name":"Ésteres de Ácidos Grasos de Sacarosa","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Emulsionante utilizado en productos alimentarios procesados para mezclar grasas y agua. Generalmente se considera seguro en las cantidades habituales de consumo.","details":"Los ésteres de ácidos grasos de sacarosa son aditivos derivados de la sacarosa y aceites vegetales, empleados como emulsionantes y estabilizantes en confitería, productos de panadería y bebidas. La evidencia disponible no muestra riesgos significativos para la población general, aunque un consumo muy elevado podría causar ligeras molestias digestivas en personas sensibles. No se asocian con alergias frecuentes y suelen estar presentes en cantidades bajas dentro de la formulación.","category":"Aditivo alimentario / emulsionante"}

dextrosa (glucosa anhidra)__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Dextrosa (glucosa Anhidra)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"La dextrosa o glucosa anhidra es un azúcar simple de rápida absorción que eleva rápidamente el nivel de azúcar en sangre.","details":"Químicamente es glucosa en forma cristalina sin agua (anhidra), con un índice glucémico muy alto. En personas con resistencia a la insulina, diabetes o síndrome metabólico, su consumo frecuente puede dificultar el control glucémico, y en la población general contribuye al exceso calórico y al aumento de riesgo de caries y sobrepeso cuando se ingiere en grandes cantidades.","category":"Azúcar añadido / carbohidrato simple"}

banana__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Banana","riskLevel":"low","summary":"La banana es una fruta natural rica en carbohidratos, potasio y fibra. Es generalmente saludable salvo en personas con alergia específica o con restricciones estrictas de carbohidratos.","details":"Aporta azúcares naturales junto con vitaminas (como vitamina B6 y vitamina C), minerales y compuestos bioactivos beneficiosos. Su contenido de fibra ayuda a la salud digestiva y a un mejor control de la glucosa en comparación con azúcares refinados, aunque sigue siendo una fuente moderada de carbohidratos. Personas con diabetes deben considerar la porción, pero en general es un ingrediente de bajo riesgo y nutritivo.","category":"Fruta"}

miel procesada__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Miel Procesada","riskLevel":"low","summary":"La miel procesada es un edulcorante natural sometido a filtrado y calentamiento, con alto contenido de azúcares simples. Su principal riesgo es contribuir al exceso de azúcares libres en la dieta.","details":"El procesamiento suele incluir calentamiento y filtrado, lo que puede reducir algunas enzimas y compuestos bioactivos presentes en la miel cruda, pero no suele implicar aditivos problemáticos. En personas sanas, su consumo moderado es generalmente seguro, aunque no se recomienda para lactantes menores de 1 año por riesgo de botulismo. Un consumo elevado puede favorecer caries, aumento de peso y descontrol glucémico en personas con diabetes o prediabetes.","category":"Edulcorante natural"}

enzimas__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Enzimas","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Proteínas que se añaden para ayudar a coagular la leche y formar el queso, como la renina o cuajo. Se usan en cantidades muy pequeñas.","details":"Las enzimas pueden ser de origen animal, microbiano o vegetal y se inactivan en gran medida durante el procesado y maduración del queso. No suelen representar un riesgo para la salud de la población general y no aportan aditivos químicos problemáticos. En personas con dietas especiales (por ejemplo, vegetarianos estrictos) puede importar el origen del cuajo, pero no por motivos de seguridad sino éticos o religiosos.","category":"Enzimas tecnológicas / Aditivo tecnológico"}

hojuelas de cebolla__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Hojuelas de Cebolla","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Las hojuelas de cebolla son cebolla deshidratada utilizada como ingrediente aromático y saborizante natural. Generalmente se consideran seguras para la mayoría de las personas.","details":"Al ser un vegetal deshidratado, aporta principalmente sabor y algunos compuestos bioactivos, pero en cantidades pequeñas dentro del producto. Puede causar molestias digestivas leves en personas sensibles a la familia de las allium (como cebolla y ajo), pero no es un alérgeno mayoritario.","category":"Vegetal / aromatizante natural"}

sabor natural__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Sabor Natural","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"El término “sabor natural” es genérico y puede abarcar una mezcla de extractos, concentrados y otros componentes derivados de fuentes naturales. Su composición exacta no suele detallarse, lo que limita la transparencia para el consumidor.","details":"Aunque por norma se considera que proviene de fuentes naturales (animales o vegetales), su procesamiento puede implicar el uso de solventes, enzimas u otros aditivos auxiliares. En personas muy sensibles o con alergias específicas, ciertos sabores naturales podrían desencadenar reacciones si provienen de alérgenos (por ejemplo, lácteos, soja o frutos secos), por lo que es un ingrediente a vigilar en dietas de eliminación o con alergias múltiples.","category":"Aromatizante / saborizante"}

extracto de cebolla__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Extracto de Cebolla","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El extracto de cebolla es un concentrado derivado de la cebolla utilizado como saborizante natural. Generalmente se considera seguro para la mayoría de las personas.","details":"Se obtiene a partir de cebollas mediante procesos de extracción y concentración, sin necesidad de aditivos artificiales. Puede causar molestias digestivas o empeorar el reflujo en personas sensibles a alimentos ricos en compuestos sulfurados. No contiene alérgenos comunes más allá de una posible sensibilidad individual a la cebolla.","category":"Saborizante natural"}

leche descremada en polvo__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Leche Descremada En Polvo","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Leche en polvo con la mayor parte de la grasa retirada, pero que sigue siendo un alérgeno lácteo. Aporta proteínas y lactosa con menos grasa que la leche entera.","details":"Aunque tiene menor contenido de grasa saturada que la leche entera en polvo, conserva las proteínas lácteas (caseína y proteínas del suero) y la lactosa, por lo que sigue siendo problemática para personas con alergia a la leche o intolerancia a la lactosa. Nutricionalmente aporta proteínas de buena calidad, calcio y otros micronutrientes, pero no es adecuada para quienes deban evitar lácteos. No se considera un aditivo, sino un ingrediente lácteo procesado.","category":"Lácteo / Alérgeno"}

color caramelo__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Color Caramelo","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Colorante alimentario que proporciona tonalidades marrones a los alimentos. Generalmente se considera seguro, aunque algunos tipos pueden formar compuestos controvertidos durante su elaboración.","details":"El color caramelo se obtiene calentando azúcares y se clasifica en varios tipos (por ejemplo, caramelo IV puede contener trazas de 4-MEI, compuesto cuya seguridad se ha debatido en altas exposiciones). En cantidades habituales en alimentos procesados, las autoridades sanitarias lo consideran seguro, pero un consumo muy elevado y frecuente de productos muy coloreados podría aumentar la exposición a estos subproductos. Algunas personas sensibles a aditivos pueden preferir limitar su ingesta, especialmente en refrescos oscuros y salsas muy procesadas.","category":"Colorante alimentario"}

glutamato monosódico__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Glutamato Monosódico","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Potenciador de sabor muy utilizado que en general se considera seguro, pero puede causar molestias en personas sensibles y suele indicar un producto muy procesado.","details":"El glutamato monosódico (MSG) realza el sabor umami y se usa de forma amplia en sopas, snacks y comidas preparadas. Las autoridades sanitarias lo consideran seguro en las cantidades habituales, pero algunas personas refieren dolor de cabeza, enrojecimiento o malestar digestivo tras consumirlo en grandes cantidades. Su presencia suele asociarse a productos con alto grado de procesamiento y contenido elevado de sodio.","category":"Potenciador de sabor / aditivo alimentario"}

soja desgrasada__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Soja Desgrasada","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Fuente de proteína vegetal, pero es un alérgeno alimentario importante y suele indicar un producto procesado.","details":"La soja desgrasada se obtiene tras extraer la mayor parte de la grasa del grano de soja, conservando una alta proporción de proteínas. Nutricionalmente puede ser beneficiosa como fuente de proteína vegetal, pero la soja es uno de los alérgenos más frecuentes y puede causar reacciones moderadas o graves en personas sensibles. Además, su uso suele aparecer en productos ultraprocesados (barras, embutidos vegetales, snacks) donde puede combinarse con otros aditivos.","category":"Proteína vegetal / posible alérgeno"}

extracto de levadura__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Extracto de Levadura","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Potenciador de sabor natural rico en compuestos umami, que puede aportar algo de sodio y suele usarse en productos procesados.","details":"El extracto de levadura se obtiene a partir de la levadura descompuesta y concentrada, y se usa para intensificar el sabor similar al caldo o a la carne. Aunque se considera seguro para la mayoría de las personas, algunas muy sensibles al glutamato pueden notar molestias porque contiene compuestos relacionados con el umami. Su presencia suele indicar alimentos procesados como caldos, sopas instantáneas, snacks salados y salsas.","category":"Potenciador de sabor / ingrediente tecnológico"}

salt__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Salt","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Salt is commonly used for seasoning and preservation but can contribute to high sodium intake when consumed in excess.","details":"Salt (sodium chloride) is essential in small amounts for fluid balance and nerve function, and it is widely used in processed foods. However, high sodium intake is linked to increased blood pressure, elevated cardiovascular risk, and fluid retention, especially in sensitive individuals. People with hypertension, kidney disease, or heart conditions are generally advised to limit sodium consumption.","category":"Mineral / Sodium source"}

corn starch__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Corn Starch","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Corn starch is a refined carbohydrate used as a thickener and texturizer in foods.","details":"Corn starch is primarily composed of carbohydrates and is generally recognized as safe for most people when used in typical culinary quantities. It offers little nutritional value beyond calories and can contribute to rapid increases in blood glucose if consumed in large amounts, which may be relevant for people with diabetes or insulin resistance. Unless an individual has a corn allergy or sensitivity, it is typically considered a low-risk ingredient.","category":"Thickener / refined carbohydrate"}

spices__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Spices","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Spices are flavoring ingredients derived from plants and are typically safe, with some potential for individual sensitivities.","details":"The term \"spices\" is generic and may include a mixture such as pepper, paprika, cumin, or others, which are commonly used for flavor and may provide beneficial phytonutrients. Most people tolerate spices well, but some individuals may experience digestive discomfort, heartburn, or allergic reactions to specific spices (for example, mustard or celery in some blends). Because the exact composition is unspecified, people with known spice allergies should exercise caution.","category":"Flavoring / seasoning"}

garlic__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Garlic","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Garlic is a natural flavoring agent with potential cardiovascular and immune benefits for most people.","details":"Garlic contains sulfur compounds and antioxidants that have been studied for possible benefits including modest blood pressure and cholesterol support, as well as antimicrobial effects. It is generally safe, though some people may experience digestive upset, gas, or heartburn, especially in larger amounts. Rarely, individuals can have a true garlic allergy or need to limit garlic if they are on certain medications that affect blood clotting or if advised by a clinician.","category":"Herb / natural flavoring"}

whole milk powder__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Whole Milk Powder","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Whole milk powder is dehydrated cow’s milk and is a significant source of dairy proteins, lactose, and milk fat, posing issues for those with dairy allergy or lactose intolerance.","details":"Whole milk powder contains casein and whey proteins, milk fat, and lactose, preserving most of the nutritional and allergenic properties of liquid milk. It is a common hidden source of dairy in processed foods and must be avoided completely by individuals with cow’s milk allergy and by those with certain dairy-related conditions. People with lactose intolerance may experience symptoms such as bloating, gas, or diarrhea depending on the amount consumed and their individual tolerance, while others can generally consume it without concern.","category":"Dairy / allergen"}

palm oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Palm Oil","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Palm oil is a common vegetable oil high in saturated fat, which can affect heart health when consumed in excess.","details":"Palm oil is widely used in processed foods because it is cheap, stable, and solid at room temperature. It is relatively high in saturated fat, and frequent intake of large amounts of saturated fat is associated with increased LDL (“bad”) cholesterol and cardiovascular risk, especially when it replaces unsaturated fats. Refined palm oil in typical food amounts is generally recognized as safe, but from a health standpoint it is better not to rely on it as a primary fat source and to balance it with healthier oils (e.g., olive, canola).","category":"Fat / Oil"}

canola oil__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Canola Oil","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Canola oil is a vegetable oil relatively low in saturated fat and higher in unsaturated fats, generally considered heart-friendly.","details":"Canola oil contains monounsaturated fats and some omega-3 fatty acids, which are usually seen as beneficial for heart health when they replace saturated fats. Refined canola oil used in processed foods is highly processed and may be exposed to high heat, which can slightly reduce some of its beneficial components, but it is still considered a comparatively healthy cooking oil. For most people, moderate intake as part of a balanced diet is considered low risk.","category":"Fat / Oil"}

soy lecithin__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Soy Lecithin","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Soy lecithin is an emulsifier derived from soy, commonly used in small amounts in processed foods and generally recognized as safe.","details":"Soy lecithin helps keep fats and water mixed in foods like chocolate, baked goods, and dressings, and is usually present in very small quantities. It is generally well tolerated, though people with soy allergies should be aware that it is soy-derived, even though it is often highly refined and may contain only trace amounts of soy protein. For the general population, it is considered a low-risk food additive.","category":"Emulsifier / Soy-derived additive"}

wheat flour__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Wheat Flour","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Wheat flour is a staple ingredient that contains gluten and can be problematic for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.","details":"Wheat flour provides carbohydrates and, depending on refinement, varying amounts of fiber and nutrients; refined white flour is lower in fiber and micronutrients than whole wheat flour. The main concern is its gluten content, which can trigger serious immune reactions in individuals with celiac disease and cause symptoms in those with non-celiac gluten sensitivity or wheat allergy. For people without these conditions, wheat flour is generally safe, but frequent use of highly refined flour can contribute to blood sugar spikes and lower overall diet quality.","category":"Grain / Gluten-containing ingredient"}

sugar__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Sugar","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Sugar is a simple carbohydrate that provides quick energy but can contribute to weight gain, tooth decay, and metabolic issues when overconsumed.","details":"Added sugars are common in processed foods and sweetened beverages and have been linked to increased risk of obesity, type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, and cardiovascular disease when intake is high. Sugar also promotes dental cavities and can drive cravings due to rapid blood glucose spikes and drops. Occasional consumption in small amounts is generally safe, but regular high intake of added sugar is considered a significant health concern.","category":"Added sweetener / Simple carbohydrate"}

natural and artificial flavors__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Natural And Artificial Flavors","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"A mixture of flavoring substances from natural and synthetic sources used to enhance taste. Safety depends on the specific compounds, which are not usually disclosed on labels.","details":"Natural and artificial flavors can include essential oils, extracts, and lab-made compounds that mimic natural tastes. While most are approved as safe at typical food-use levels, they can sometimes trigger sensitivities in susceptible individuals, and the lack of transparency makes it difficult for consumers with allergies or chemical sensitivities to fully assess risk.","category":"Flavoring agents"}

honey__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Honey","riskLevel":"low","summary":"A natural sweetener produced by bees, composed mainly of fructose and glucose. It is generally safe for most people but should not be given to infants under one year old.","details":"Honey provides simple sugars and small amounts of antioxidants and trace minerals, but it is still a concentrated source of sugar and calories that can affect blood glucose and dental health. It can contain spores of Clostridium botulinum, which is why it is contraindicated for infants, though it is safe for older children and adults when consumed in moderation.","category":"Natural sweetener"}

dextrin__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Dextrin","riskLevel":"low","summary":"A group of short-chain carbohydrates derived from starch, used as a thickener, stabilizer, or fiber source. It is generally recognized as safe for most consumers.","details":"Dextrin is usually produced from corn, wheat, or other starches and is easily digestible, contributing mainly carbohydrates and sometimes a small amount of functional fiber. People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should be aware that wheat-derived dextrin can contain gluten unless specifically labeled gluten-free.","category":"Carbohydrate additive / thickener"}

pasteurized milk__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Pasteurized Milk","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Heat-treated cow’s milk used as a base dairy ingredient, which reduces microbial risk. It is nutritious but is a common allergen and contains lactose.","details":"Pasteurization kills most pathogenic bacteria while preserving proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals such as calcium and vitamin B12. However, milk proteins (casein and whey) can cause allergic reactions, and the lactose content can trigger digestive symptoms in people with lactose intolerance, making it a concern for those with dairy-related conditions.","category":"Dairy allergen"}

cheese cultures__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Cheese Cultures","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Beneficial bacterial cultures used in cheese making to develop flavor and texture. They are generally safe and common in fermented dairy products.","details":"Cheese cultures typically include strains of lactic acid bacteria that ferment lactose into lactic acid, helping preserve the product and contribute tangy flavors. These microbes are considered safe for most people and can have mild probiotic-like effects, though individuals with severe dairy allergies should still avoid products containing them because they are part of a dairy-based matrix.","category":"Fermentation cultures / dairy"}

alkali (alkalizing agent e.g. sodium car.analysis: {"name":"Alkali (alkalizing Agent, E.g., Sodium Carbonate / Potassium Carbonate)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Alkali refers to alkaline substances used to adjust acidity or process foods, such as cocoa or noodles. At typical food levels, these agents are generally considered safe for most people.","details":"In food, alkalis (like sodium carbonate, potassium carbonate, or similar bases) are used to raise pH, modify texture, or enhance color, for example in Dutch-processed cocoa or ramen noodles. The main concern is that some alkalis can contribute to overall sodium or mineral intake, which could matter for individuals on restricted-sodium or kidney-healthy diets. For the general population consuming normal amounts of processed foods, the toxicological risk of approved food-grade alkalis is low.","category":"processing aid / pH regulator"}

tomato extract__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Tomato Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Tomato extract is a concentrated form of tomatoes used for flavor, color, and nutrients like lycopene. It is generally considered safe and can even provide beneficial antioxidants.","details":"Tomato extract is produced by concentrating tomato solids, often preserving natural compounds such as lycopene, vitamins, and organic acids. It is commonly used in sauces, soups, and snacks for a strong tomato flavor and red color, without relying on artificial colorants. Unless someone has a specific allergy or sensitivity to tomatoes or nightshades, it poses very low health risk and can contribute useful phytonutrients.","category":"natural flavor / vegetable concentrate"}

soy protein__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Soy Protein","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Soy protein is a concentrated protein derived from soybeans, widely used in meat alternatives and processed foods. It is nutritious but is a major allergen and can be problematic for people with soy allergy or intolerance.","details":"Soy protein (concentrate or isolate) provides a high-quality plant protein and is generally safe for most consumers when eaten in typical amounts. However, soy is one of the top food allergens, and even small amounts can trigger reactions ranging from mild symptoms to severe anaphylaxis in sensitive individuals. People with thyroid issues or on certain medications may also wish to moderate high intakes of processed soy, though food-regulatory agencies regard normal dietary levels as safe.","category":"protein source / major allergen"}

protein hydrolysate (hydrolysate)__food_.analysis: {"name":"Protein Hydrolysate (hydrolysate)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Hydrolysate usually refers to protein hydrolysate, where proteins are broken into smaller peptides and amino acids. This improves digestibility and flavor but can sometimes include or generate flavor enhancers similar to MSG.","details":"Protein hydrolysates are produced by enzymatic or chemical breakdown of proteins from sources such as soy, wheat, milk, or other plants/animals, and are used to enhance flavor and improve texture. Because hydrolysis releases free glutamate, some hydrolysates (e.g., hydrolyzed vegetable protein) can act similarly to monosodium glutamate (MSG), which some individuals report sensitivity to, though evidence of broad harm is limited. Allergen risk depends on the original protein source (e.g., soy, wheat, milk), which is not specified here, so people with known allergies should check labeling carefully.","category":"flavor enhancer / protein derivative"}

apple puree__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Apple Puree","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Apple puree is a mashed or blended form of apples used as a fruit base, sweetener, or texture ingredient. It is generally safe and can provide fiber and natural sugars.","details":"Apple puree is typically made from cooked or raw apples that are blended into a smooth consistency, sometimes with peel and sometimes without. It contributes natural sweetness, some fiber, and phytonutrients such as polyphenols, depending on how it is processed. The primary concerns are for individuals with apple or birch-pollen–related oral allergy syndrome, or for those who need to limit simple sugars, but for most consumers it is a low-risk, minimally processed fruit ingredient.","category":"fruit ingredient / natural sweetener"}

soy sauce (from soybean)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Soy Sauce (from Soybean)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Soy sauce is a fermented seasoning made from soybeans that is high in sodium and is a common soy allergen.","details":"Traditional soy sauce provides umami flavor but typically contains a high amount of salt, which can contribute to elevated blood pressure if consumed in excess. It is a major source of soy, a top food allergen that can trigger reactions in sensitive individuals. Some soy sauces may also contain gluten depending on how they are made, which is important for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.","category":"Condiment / Allergen (soy, possible gluten) / High-sodium ingredient"}

wheat__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Wheat","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Wheat is a common grain and a major source of gluten, a key allergen and trigger for celiac disease. It is generally safe for most people but must be strictly avoided by those with celiac disease or wheat/gluten allergy or intolerance.","details":"As a gluten-containing grain, wheat can cause serious intestinal damage and systemic symptoms in people with celiac disease, requiring complete avoidance. It can also provoke allergic reactions or non-celiac gluten sensitivity, leading to symptoms like bloating, rashes, or respiratory issues. For the general population, wheat is not inherently harmful, but it is a mandated allergen on labels and relevant for anyone following gluten-free diets.","category":"Cereal grain / Allergen (gluten, wheat)"}

garlic extract__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Garlic Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Garlic extract is a concentrated form of garlic used for flavor and potential health benefits. It is generally safe, though it may cause digestive discomfort in sensitive individuals.","details":"Garlic extract provides the characteristic garlic flavor without the bulk of whole garlic and may retain some bioactive compounds with antioxidant and antimicrobial properties. From a food safety perspective, it is not associated with common problematic additives, artificial colors, or sweeteners. However, some people experience heartburn, gas, or other gastrointestinal discomfort with garlic, and a small number may have garlic sensitivity or allergy.","category":"Natural flavoring / Spice extract"}

tomato powder__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Tomato Powder","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Tomato powder is a dehydrated and ground form of tomatoes used for flavor and color. It is usually safe and considered a natural ingredient, though it may be an issue for people with tomato allergy or reflux.","details":"Tomato powder concentrates the natural acids, flavors, and pigments of tomatoes without introducing synthetic additives by itself. It can contribute natural color and umami taste and may retain some vitamins and antioxidants such as lycopene, depending on processing. Individuals with tomato allergy or severe acid reflux may need to limit or avoid it, but for most consumers it does not pose notable additive, allergen (beyond tomato itself), or artificial ingredient concerns.","category":"Dehydrated vegetable / Natural flavor and color"}

dried onion__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Dried Onion","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Dried onion is a dehydrated form of onion used as a natural flavoring. It is generally safe, with concerns mainly for those with onion sensitivity or digestive issues.","details":"As a simple dehydrated vegetable ingredient, dried onion does not typically involve artificial colors, preservatives, or sweeteners by default. It provides natural savory flavor and some phytonutrients, though many heat-sensitive compounds are reduced during processing. A subset of people with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) or FODMAP sensitivity may experience gas, bloating, or discomfort from onions, but there are no major additive or trans fat concerns associated with this ingredient itself.","category":"Dehydrated vegetable / Natural flavoring"}

tomato paste__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Tomato Paste","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Tomato paste is a concentrated form of tomatoes and is generally safe for most people. It mainly contains natural sugars, fiber, vitamins, and antioxidants like lycopene.","details":"Tomato paste is made by cooking down tomatoes to remove much of the water, concentrating the flavor and nutrients. It is naturally rich in vitamin C, potassium, and lycopene, an antioxidant linked with heart and eye health. Potential concerns are mainly for individuals with tomato allergies or acid reflux, as its acidity can sometimes worsen heartburn.","category":"Whole food ingredient"}

fermented milk__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Fermented Milk","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Fermented milk is a dairy product that has been cultured with beneficial bacteria and is usually safe but can be problematic for those with dairy allergies or lactose intolerance. It may support gut health due to probiotic content.","details":"Fermented milk (such as yogurt-like bases or cultured milk drinks) is produced by adding specific bacteria to milk, which partially break down lactose and form lactic acid. This process can improve digestibility for some people and contribute beneficial bacteria that may support gut microbiota. However, it still contains milk proteins (like casein and whey) and residual lactose, making it unsuitable for people with milk allergy and potentially troublesome for those with lactose intolerance or dairy sensitivity.","category":"Dairy / allergen"}

citric acid__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Citric Acid","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Citric acid is a common food acidulant and preservative used to add tartness and improve shelf life. It is generally recognized as safe for most people at typical food levels.","details":"Citric acid is usually produced by fermenting sugar with specific molds and is widely used in beverages, candies, sauces, and processed foods to enhance flavor and control pH. For most people it poses little risk, though in high concentrations it can irritate the mouth or stomach, and a small number of individuals report sensitivity or irritation from frequent exposure. It does not contribute to artificial sweetener, trans fat, or MSG-related concerns, but it does signal that the product is somewhat processed.","category":"Acidulant / preservative"}

mono- and diglycerides__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Mono- And Diglycerides","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Mono- and diglycerides are emulsifiers used to improve texture and shelf life in processed foods. They are generally allowed in food but can be a hidden source of industrial trans fats depending on how they are made.","details":"Mono- and diglycerides are partial breakdown products of fats that help oil and water mix, commonly used in baked goods, ice creams, and many processed foods. While considered safe by regulators, they are often derived from vegetable oils that may be partially hydrogenated, which can introduce small amounts of industrial trans fats not always reflected on nutrition labels. For people aiming to minimize processed additives or trans fat intake, frequent consumption of products containing these emulsifiers may be a concern, though occasional intake is unlikely to pose major health risks.","category":"Emulsifier / processed fat derivative"}

cocoa powder (processed with alkali)__fo.analysis: {"name":"Cocoa Powder (processed With Alkali)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Cocoa powder processed with alkali, also called Dutch-processed cocoa, is generally safe for most people when consumed in normal food amounts. The alkalizing process reduces acidity and can slightly lower some antioxidant content.","details":"Dutch-processing uses alkaline salts to neutralize cocoa’s natural acidity, improving color and flavor but modestly decreasing certain polyphenol antioxidants compared to natural cocoa. It still contains naturally occurring caffeine and theobromine, which may be a concern in large amounts for sensitive individuals, but typical dietary use in foods and beverages is considered safe. People with cocoa allergy or intolerance should avoid it regardless of processing method.","category":"Cocoa and chocolate ingredient"}

enzymes__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Enzymes","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Enzymes are proteins used to modify food properties, aid processing, or improve texture and flavor. They are generally considered safe but can pose issues for people with specific allergies to the enzyme source.","details":"Food enzymes (such as amylases, proteases, lipases, etc.) are commonly derived from microbial, plant, or animal sources and are used in baking, dairy, and other processed foods. While the enzymes themselves are typically nontoxic and are often inactivated by heat, sensitive individuals could react if they are allergic to the original source (e.g., certain molds or animal products). Because labels usually list them generically as “enzymes,” it can be difficult for consumers with rare enzyme or source allergies to identify the exact type used.","category":"processing aid"}

onion flake__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Onion Flake","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Onion flake is simply dehydrated onion used for flavoring and is generally safe for most people. It can cause digestive discomfort for those sensitive to onions or with certain gastrointestinal conditions.","details":"Dehydrated onion retains the sulfur compounds and FODMAPs (fermentable carbohydrates) present in fresh onion, which can trigger gas, bloating, or pain in individuals with IBS or onion intolerance. Apart from these sensitivities, onion flake is a natural ingredient with antioxidant compounds and is not associated with typical additive-related concerns such as artificial colors, flavors, or preservatives.","category":"herb / spice / vegetable"}

natural flavor__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Natural Flavor","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Natural flavor is a broad term for flavoring substances derived from natural sources but often highly processed. It is generally recognized as safe, yet its vague labeling can conceal potential allergens or animal-derived components.","details":"Under regulations, “natural flavor” can come from plant or animal sources and may include concentrates, extracts, and distillates, often processed with solvents or carriers. Manufacturers are not required to specify the exact source on the ingredient list, which can be problematic for people with allergies (e.g., to certain fruits, spices, or animal products) or strict dietary preferences (e.g., vegan, religious restrictions). While safety assessments for typical consumption are reassuring, the lack of transparency and potential for hidden allergens or additives justifies a moderate risk classification for sensitive individuals.","category":"flavoring"}

onion extract__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Onion Extract","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Onion extract is a concentrated flavoring derived from onions and is generally safe for most people. It may cause issues for those with onion allergies or sensitivity to onion’s sulfur compounds.","details":"This ingredient is typically produced by extracting flavor compounds from onions using water or other approved solvents, then concentrating them. It delivers strong onion flavor without bulk but can still contain allergenic and FODMAP components similar to whole onion, potentially provoking symptoms in sensitive individuals or those with IBS. For the general population, it does not pose concerns associated with artificial additives, colorants, or preservatives.","category":"flavoring / vegetable extract"}

dried (processing descriptor not a speci.analysis: {"name":"Dried (processing Descriptor, Not a Specific Ingredient)","riskLevel":"low","summary":"“Dried” describes the physical state of an ingredient and is not a standalone ingredient. It generally does not pose a health risk by itself.","details":"In ingredient lists, the word “dried” usually precedes a food (e.g., dried garlic, dried onion) to indicate that moisture has been removed for preservation and concentration of flavor. Without the accompanying food name, this term is incomplete, but the drying process itself is a standard, low‑risk food preservation method unless additional additives are used, which are not specified here.","category":"Processing descriptor"}

maltose__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Maltose","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Maltose is a simple sugar used as a sweetener and carbohydrate source. For most people it is safe in normal food amounts but contributes to total sugar intake.","details":"Maltose is a disaccharide composed of two glucose molecules and is used in processed foods for mild sweetness and texture. While it does not contain fructose, it can raise blood glucose levels and should be limited by individuals with diabetes, insulin resistance, or those monitoring overall sugar consumption. Excess intake of maltose and other added sugars may contribute to weight gain, dental cavities, and metabolic issues over time.","category":"Sugar / sweetener"}

whey powder__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Whey Powder","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Whey powder is a dairy-derived protein and lactose source commonly used in processed foods. It is safe for most people but is a concern for those with milk allergy or lactose intolerance.","details":"Whey powder is made from the liquid portion of milk left after cheese production and contains proteins (such as whey protein concentrate) along with varying amounts of lactose. It is a complete protein and generally considered safe, but it is a major allergen for individuals with cow’s milk allergy and can cause symptoms like hives, digestive upset, or anaphylaxis. People with lactose intolerance may also experience gas, bloating, or diarrhea, especially if large amounts are consumed or if other lactose sources are present.","category":"Dairy / allergen"}

garlic flake__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Garlic Flake","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Garlic flake is simply dehydrated garlic used as a flavoring. It is generally safe and can have beneficial properties, though it may cause digestive discomfort in some sensitive individuals.","details":"Garlic flakes are made from sliced, dried garlic and provide the characteristic garlic aroma and flavor without additives. Garlic has been associated with potential cardiovascular and antimicrobial benefits, though these depend on dose and preparation. A minority of people may experience gastrointestinal irritation, heartburn, or odor issues, and those with a true garlic allergy (rare) should avoid it.","category":"Herb / spice"}

paprika color__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Paprika Color","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Paprika color is a natural coloring derived from paprika peppers, used to give foods a red to orange hue. It is generally considered safe, especially compared to artificial colorants.","details":"Paprika color is typically extracted from Capsicum annuum (paprika) and standardized for carotenoid pigments like capsanthin and capsorubin. As a natural colorant, it is usually preferable to synthetic dyes (such as Red 40), although highly refined extracts may contain minimal actual spice. Rarely, individuals sensitive to peppers or with certain allergies might react, but adverse effects are uncommon at typical food-use levels.","category":"Natural color / spice extract"}

glucose__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Glucose","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Glucose is a simple sugar used as a sweetener and energy source. In large amounts it can contribute to excess calorie intake and blood sugar spikes.","details":"Glucose is a monosaccharide that is rapidly absorbed and can cause sharp increases in blood sugar, which is particularly relevant for people with insulin resistance or diabetes. Frequent intake of products high in added glucose may promote weight gain, dental caries, and increased cardiometabolic risk when part of an overall high-sugar diet. In normal quantities within a balanced diet, it is generally recognized as safe.","category":"Added sugar / sweetener"}

sucrose fatty acid esters__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Sucrose Fatty Acid Esters","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Sucrose fatty acid esters are emulsifiers made from sucrose and fatty acids. They are widely used to improve texture and mixing of ingredients in processed foods.","details":"These compounds help oil and water mix, stabilizing products like baked goods, desserts, and certain beverages. Safety evaluations by regulatory authorities have generally found them to be of low toxicity at typical dietary intakes, though very high experimental doses may cause mild gastrointestinal effects. For most consumers, occasional consumption in processed foods is considered low risk.","category":"Emulsifier / food additive"}

dextrose anhydrous (glucose)__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Dextrose Anhydrous (glucose)","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Dextrose anhydrous is a simple sugar (glucose) used as a sweetener and energy source in foods. It is generally recognized as safe, but excessive intake of added sugars can contribute to health issues.","details":"Dextrose anhydrous is a purified form of glucose with the water removed, commonly derived from corn and used to sweeten products or adjust texture and fermentation. For most healthy individuals it is safe in normal dietary amounts, but high consumption of simple sugars is linked to weight gain, blood sugar spikes, and increased risk of metabolic diseases such as type 2 diabetes. People with diabetes or impaired glucose tolerance should monitor intake carefully, as it rapidly raises blood glucose levels.","category":"Sugar / Sweetener"}

banana__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Banana","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Banana is a whole fruit ingredient that provides natural sugars, fiber, and micronutrients. It is generally considered a healthy, minimally processed food component.","details":"Bananas supply potassium, vitamin B6, and some dietary fiber, along with natural fructose and glucose. For most people, bananas are a beneficial part of a balanced diet, though those on very strict carbohydrate-controlled plans or with specific medical conditions (e.g., certain kidney issues requiring potassium restriction) may need to monitor intake. When used instead of refined sugars, banana can improve the nutritional quality of a product.","category":"Whole fruit / natural ingredient"}

processed honey__food__en.analysis: {"name":"Processed Honey","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Processed honey is a refined form of honey that is primarily a natural sugar source with some minor bioactive compounds. Processing can reduce some beneficial components while maintaining a high sugar content.","details":"Honey is mostly fructose and glucose, and even when processed, it retains a similar caloric and glycemic impact to other sugars, though sometimes slightly lower glycemic than pure glucose. Heat treatment and filtration can reduce enzymes and antioxidants compared to raw honey, making it functionally closer to a regular sweetener. Overconsumption, especially in processed foods, may contribute to weight gain, elevated blood sugars, and dental caries, so it should be used in moderation even though it is often perceived as more natural.","category":"Natural sweetener / added sugar"}

玉米淀粉__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"玉米淀粉","riskLevel":"low","summary":"玉米淀粉是一种从玉米中提取的常见增稠剂和填充剂，一般被认为对大多数人是安全的。","details":"玉米淀粉主要成分是碳水化合物，用于增稠酱汁、汤类和改善食品口感，不含人工色素或防腐剂。对玉米或其蛋白过敏的人需谨慎，但玉米淀粉中蛋白含量极低，多数情况下耐受良好。对于需要控制血糖的人，应注意整体饮食中精制淀粉的摄入量。","category":"增稠剂/稳定剂"}

香辛料（香料/香料混合物）__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"香辛料（香料/香料混合物）","riskLevel":"low","summary":"“香辛料”通常指天然香料和香辛植物的混合物，一般安全，但成分不够明确。","details":"配料表中标注为“香辛料”或“香料”的成分，通常是多种天然香料或香辛植物的混合，例如胡椒、辣椒、孜然等。大多数人群适量食用是安全的，但具体种类和用量不透明，敏感人群（如对某些香料、花椒、辣椒过敏或有胃肠道疾病者）可能需要留意食用后的反应。对极度过敏体质的人，建议仅将其视为“成分不完全明确”的轻微潜在风险来源。","category":"香辛料/调味料"}

大蒜__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"大蒜","riskLevel":"low","summary":"大蒜是一种常见的天然调味食材和香辛料，对大多数人来说较为安全。具有一定抗氧化和抗菌作用。","details":"大蒜不属于人工添加剂、不含人工色素或甜味剂，也与反式脂肪和高果糖糖浆无关。少数人可能出现胃部不适或口气加重，但通常与严重过敏关系不大。对正在服用抗凝药物或有胃溃疡的人，长期大量摄入需咨询医生。","category":"天然香辛料"}

全脂奶粉__food__zh.analysis: {"name":"全脂奶粉","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"全脂奶粉是以牛奶为原料喷雾干燥得到的乳制品，含有乳糖和乳蛋白。对于乳制品过敏或乳糖不耐受人群存在一定风险。","details":"全脂奶粉属于天然乳制品成分，不是人工甜味剂或防腐剂，但同时也是常见食物过敏原之一，可能引起皮疹、腹泻、呼吸困难等过敏反应。乳糖不耐受者食用后容易出现胀气、腹痛和腹泻等胃肠道不适。其本身钠含量通常不高，但总能量和饱和脂肪相对较高，需注意控制摄入量。","category":"乳制品/常见过敏原"}

aceite de palma__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Aceite de Palma","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"El aceite de palma es una grasa vegetal muy usada en productos ultraprocesados, a menudo con alto contenido de grasas saturadas. Su consumo frecuente puede contribuir a elevar el colesterol LDL, especialmente en dietas poco equilibradas.","details":"Nutricionalmente aporta grasas saturadas que, en exceso, se asocian con mayor riesgo cardiovascular, sobre todo cuando sustituye a grasas insaturadas más saludables. En productos industriales puede estar refinado a alta temperatura, lo que puede generar compuestos indeseables si se abusa de ellos, aunque dentro de los límites de seguridad regulatoria. El impacto ambiental de su producción también es controvertido, aunque no afecta directamente a la salud del consumidor.","category":"Grasa vegetal refinada"}

aceite de canola__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Aceite de Canola","riskLevel":"low","summary":"El aceite de canola es un aceite vegetal con contenido relativamente bajo en grasas saturadas y mayor proporción de grasas monoinsaturadas y poliinsaturadas. Se considera generalmente una opción de grasa más saludable en comparación con otros aceites ricos en grasas saturadas.","details":"En su forma refinada, se usa frecuentemente en alimentos procesados por su sabor neutro y buena estabilidad. Puede contener pequeñas cantidades de grasas trans formadas durante el refinado, pero en niveles normalmente bajos y regulados. El principal factor de riesgo está más relacionado con el exceso de calorías y el uso en alimentos ultraprocesados que con el aceite de canola en sí.","category":"Grasa y aceite vegetal"}

lecitina de soja__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Lecitina de Soja","riskLevel":"low","summary":"La lecitina de soja es un emulsionante derivado de la soja utilizado para mezclar grasas y agua en alimentos procesados. Se usa en pequeñas cantidades y se considera generalmente segura para la mayoría de las personas.","details":"Actúa como estabilizante en chocolates, productos de panadería y margarinas, mejorando textura y conservación sin aportar una cantidad significativa de grasa o calorías en la porción final. Puede contener trazas de proteínas de soja, por lo que personas con alergia a la soja deben tener precaución, aunque el riesgo suele ser menor que con otros derivados de soja menos procesados. Las agencias de seguridad alimentaria la consideran un aditivo de bajo riesgo en los niveles habituales de uso.","category":"Emulsionante / Aditivo alimentario"}

harina de trigo__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Harina de Trigo","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"La harina de trigo es una fuente básica de carbohidratos y contiene gluten, un alérgeno común. Es adecuada para la mayoría de las personas, pero problemática para quienes tienen enfermedad celíaca, sensibilidad al gluten o alergia al trigo.","details":"El principal riesgo de la harina de trigo radica en su contenido de gluten, que puede desencadenar reacciones inmunitarias graves en personas con enfermedad celíaca y molestias digestivas en quienes presentan sensibilidad al gluten no celíaca. Además, como carbohidrato refinado, su consumo frecuente en grandes cantidades puede contribuir al aumento de peso y a picos de glucosa en sangre. No suele contener aditivos peligrosos por sí misma, pero es un alérgeno prioritario que siempre debe ser identificado claramente en la etiqueta.","category":"Cereal con gluten / Alérgeno"}

azúcar__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Azúcar","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"El azúcar es un endulzante calórico que aporta energía rápida pero ningún valor nutricional significativo. El consumo elevado y frecuente se asocia con mayor riesgo de caries, sobrepeso y trastornos metabólicos.","details":"En cantidades moderadas, el azúcar es generalmente seguro para la población sana, pero su abuso se relaciona con resistencia a la insulina, aumento de riesgo de diabetes tipo 2, hígado graso no alcohólico y enfermedades cardiovasculares. También puede favorecer la aparición de caries dentales y contribuir al desequilibrio del apetito por su impacto en los picos de glucosa e insulina. Es recomendable vigilar la cantidad total de azúcares añadidos en la dieta diaria.","category":"Endulzante calórico"}

álcali (proceso con álcali)__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Álcali (proceso Con Álcali)","riskLevel":"bajo","summary":"El término “álcali” en alimentos suele indicar que un ingrediente (por ejemplo, cacao) fue procesado con una sustancia alcalina para ajustar el pH. En cantidades usadas en alimentos es generalmente seguro para la mayoría de las personas.","details":"Los álcalis alimentarios más comunes son carbonato de potasio, bicarbonato de sodio u otros reguladores de acidez autorizados. Su función principal es modificar la acidez, el color y el sabor, no aportar nutrientes. El riesgo puede aumentar ligeramente en personas que necesitan limitar el sodio o ciertos minerales, pero en consumidores sanos se considera de bajo riesgo en las dosis habituales.","category":"regulador de acidez / procesamiento"}

extracto de tomate__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Extracto de Tomate","riskLevel":"low","summary":"Ingrediente derivado del tomate concentrado, generalmente seguro para la mayoría de las personas.","details":"El extracto de tomate aporta licopeno, antioxidantes y compuestos vegetales beneficiosos, aunque en forma concentrada. Suele usarse como saborizante y colorante natural, sin aditivos artificiales añadidos, pero puede contribuir ligeramente a la acidez del producto.","category":"Ingrediente vegetal / derivado de tomate"}

proteína de soja__food__es.analysis: {"name":"Proteína de Soja","riskLevel":"moderate","summary":"Fuente concentrada de proteína derivada de la soja, con buen perfil de aminoácidos. Principal preocupación: es un alérgeno común.","details":"La proteína de soja es muy utilizada en productos procesados como sustituto de la carne o para aumentar el contenido proteico. Para la mayoría de las personas es segura, pero puede desencadenar reacciones alérgicas importantes en individuos sensibles a la soja. En personas sin alergia, su consumo moderado se considera generalmente seguro dentro de una dieta equilibrada.","category":"Proteína vegetal / Alérgeno (soja)"}
